facts.value: The University of Limerick has participated in the ERASMUS programme since 1988.
The University of Limerick has links with over 300 partner institutions throughout Europe.
The University of Limerick had been awarded the Best Erasmus Programme award by the Irish Education Awards in 2018, 2019, 2022, 2024 and 2025.
UL has the largest outgoing cohort in Ireland with approx. 600 UL students studying abroad at European partner institutions each year.

The following UL degree programmes have a compulsory semester abroad: Arts (LM002), Social Sciences (LM019), Applied Languages (LM044), European Studies (LM040), International Business (LM056), Psychology & Sociology (LM038), Global Politics (LM030), Journalism & Digital Communication (LM039), Psychology (LM102).
During the semester abroad, students remain full-time registered students of UL and do not pay tuition fees at the host University.
Students studying in Programme countries may receive an EU mobility grant to assist with the added cost of living abroad.
The EU mobility grant should not affect any other local grant funding, for example, the SUSI grant.
Information sessions on the Erasmus programme are held each semester.
Each degree programme has an Erasmus Academic Coordinator, who can arrange information sessions and provide individual advice.
UL students who wish to participate in the Erasmus programme can contact UL Global at outgoing.erasmus@ul.ie for further information.
